title: A run exits on stops that only need resuming: make continuing mechanical
description:
On 2026-09-19/20 the operator's orchestrator restarted epic runs BY HAND about fifteen times across ncv and dha. Almost every restart was the same act — the run stopped, and something typed  again with identical arguments. The run then adopted its in-flight attempts by identity and carried on.

That is not a decision. It is a loop the orchestrator is performing on the run's behalf, and every one of today's long stalls happened in it: a run sat dead for two hours overnight and another for two hours this morning, both times because the party that had to retype the command was doing something else. The Phase 3 retro already said every stall traced to the monitoring layer rather than to ticfac; this is the mechanism behind that sentence.

THE DISTINCTION THAT MATTERS: stops are of two kinds, and the run does not separate them.
  - RESUMABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: an attempt settled and was rejected with nothing lost; a transient remote failure (enj); a tracker width refusal (3mp); a gate that failed and whose tree has since changed. Nothing about these needs a person — the next incarnation adopts, re-derives and continues.
  - NEEDS A PERSON: a finding to triage (aqm moves this to one point), a gate that fails on an unchanged tree, a refusal naming work only a human can judge. These are decisions, and stopping for them is correct.

Work:
- A supervised mode that keeps going across the first kind, with bounded backoff and a cap, and stops for the second — reporting which kind it saw and why. Not a shell loop around the binary: the run knows which refusals are resumable and the shell does not.
- Every automatic continuation must be RECORDED as one: a resume nobody typed is still an intervention in the count zi2 asks for, and an epic that 'completed unattended' after forty automatic resumes has not demonstrated what the gate claims.
- The cap is the safety: a run that resumes forever over the same refusal is a spin, not progress. Stop, and say what it stopped over.

Related: zi2 (count interventions mechanically), aqm (fewer stops of the second kind), enj and 3mp (two stop kinds already shown resumable).
notes: 2026-09-20 12:15 - Correction: a shell-quoting slip ate two words. The second paragraph should read "something typed `ticfac run-epic ...` again with identical arguments."
acceptance_criteria: A run continues across resumable stops without a person retyping the command, stops for decisions, records every automatic continuation as an intervention, and cannot spin: a repeated refusal over an unchanged tree halts with the reason
